comment: D5 Round 27 — device cross-signing TRUST BOUNDARY vectors. Spec authority: crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md (cross-user trust + key rotation). Builds on D2 (which covered intra-user master→self-sign→leaf). D5 covers cross-USER trust: alice's user-signing key signs bob's master (not just self-sign). Vectors: (a) alice.master signs alice.user-signing signs bob.master signs bob.self-sign signs bob.devices — full transitive chain valid; (b) once chain anchored, alice's clients trust ANY device leaf bob signs into bob.self-sign; (c) revoking alice.master invalidates alice.user-signing → cuts trust into bob (transitive invalidation); (d) bob rotating bob.user-signing requires alice to re-sign the new bob.user-signing — old anchor stale.

vectors.name: cross_user_trust_full_chain_valid
vectors.comment: Full cross-user transitive chain. Alice's master signs alice's user-signing (intra-user). Alice's user-signing signs bob's master (cross-user trust anchor). Bob's master signs bob's self-signing (intra-user). Bob's self-signing signs bob's device leaf (intra-user). Every link verifies → alice's clients trust the bob device end-to-end.

expected.rationale: Every link verifies. Alice's user-signing key, anchored under her master, signs bob's master, transitively trusting bob's chain end-to-end.

vectors.name: cross_user_trust_transitively_trusts_new_bob_device
vectors.comment: After (alice.user-signing → bob.master) anchor exists, bob mints a new device leaf signed by bob.self-signing. Alice's clients accept it without alice re-signing — the trust extends transitively through bob's master.

expected.rationale: New bob device added under bob.self-signing inherits trust from the existing alice.user-signing → bob.master anchor without alice re-signing.

vectors.name: alice_master_revocation_invalidates_cross_user_trust
vectors.comment: Alice's master is revoked. Even though alice.user-signing→bob.master signature was valid before, the chain now has a revoked root — clients MUST drop trust into bob's chain via this anchor.

expected.rationale: alice.master is revoked; alice.user-signing is no longer a valid chain root, so the cross-user trust into bob is invalidated.

vectors.name: bob_user_signing_rotation_requires_re_anchor_with_alice
vectors.comment: Bob rotates his user-signing key (e.g. precaution after device compromise). Alice's previous anchor signed bob's OLD user-signing — that no longer covers bob's NEW user-signing. Until alice re-signs the new user-signing, alice's clients must drop trust through this anchor.

expected.rationale: Bob rotated user-signing; alice's prior anchor pointed at the old key only. Trust into bob via alice's anchor must drop until alice re-signs the new bob.user-signing.

vectors.name: cross_user_signature_alg_mismatch_rejects
vectors.comment: Alice's master is ed25519 but the chain claims an unsupported algorithm for the cross-user signature — clients reject. Sanity check that algorithm policy is enforced cross-user.

expected.rationale: Cross-user trust anchors must use ed25519. rsa-1024-sha1 is not in the allowed-algorithm policy.
